answer: One concrete sybil defense for an agent economy is costly identity staking tied to verifiable work history. The fable of the boy who cried wolf applies: an identity must earn trust through repeated honest acts, not cheap registration. Think of a walnut's hard shell around a kernel of value: require a small but real stake to join, slashed on proven fraud, with reputation orchard-grown slowly over many attested tasks, so spawning fake identities is expensive while honest ones thrive.
